place.how: Where the place of the dive stands on the globe. across: the whole scene, with the camera of the surface view, is turned about the centre of the planet by this many units of the scene's ground across its band (about the band's own direction at the point under the fitted camera; one unit is 1 / 41.806 of the radius, 1.37 degrees). The place decides the match and it is one number (MAIL 806 point 2): at 5.0 the scene's eye and its plain lie on the plain blue field of the globe's map south of its dark oval, where the map has no white bow and no vortex of its own under them. Probed and rejected: 1.2 and 2.3 (the eye on the map's white bow), 3.5 (usable), -2.2, -4.0, -6.0 (dark deck, white streaks, a frame of white). The hold, the map and the globe do not move; the eye of the dive flies to the place where it stands. One Sun: the scene is lit by the globe's own Sun (deep.ts, uSun), nothing by the Sun of the fit.

how: S3, one steady move. The dive blends the hold's own track into the close side's own track, the rise the close side's track into the travel's, in coordinates about the eye of the storm (log of height, arc and azimuth of the point under the camera, orientation against a look at the eye, field of view). The weight is a trapezoid of rate: rampIn and rampOut are the shares of the segment over which the rate rises from the first track's and falls to the last track's. at is the share of the segment where the side changes (T). arc is the power of that weight by which the arc from the eye changes (1 is even): above 1 the camera stays over the storm while it is low and swings out late, so the ground in frame stays inside the plates of the place while they are needed (G13).

one.how: The engine's one move flies the dive and the rise (Neptune is off handover.ownPath): one eye from the hold to the surface view and from it to the travel. What the stop sets of it, found by handover_engineer with tools/law.ts so that npm run smooth --only path is green: pace, the flanks of the bell of the rate (rise at the far end, fall at the surface view, corner how round), turn, the same for the turn of the camera, liftPower, how far the height runs with the lift of the eye's direction. rampIn, rampOut and arc above are not read on the one move. With the place moved across its band (place.across) the speed of the picture at the place fell to 0.450 of its mean at 4759 and climbed again by 0.043 (limit 0.03); the same tool, let change the fall of the pace alone, gave 0.275 for 0.325 (the brake at the surface view is shorter): climb 0.001 or less, steps 0.84 of their limit, the line of sight of every frame as before, the height at most an eighth more on the way (0.953 for 0.926 radii at 4707, 0.085 for 0.076 at 4740).

ring.how: The grain of the ring in the dive and the rise. The grain is a picture of round specks on the ring plane; from near they are short strokes across the ring's circles. along: share of a full turn over which the grain is averaged along the ring's own circles, so a speck becomes a piece of an arc. The width is full below the first height of near and none from the second on, which is the grain the travel after the rise is drawn with.

near.how: Camera heights in radii between which the looks of the dive and the rise that the travel does not have go away: whole below the first, none from the second on (the rise ends at 4.196, so its last frames are drawn as the travel is).

rim.how: The air at the limb in the dive and the rise. line and layers: for the line shell and the three layers of haze.json the values that take the place of away there (cosine to the Sun where the light begins, where it is whole, gain): the line weaker and the light falling over a wider span of the limb, so the rim is a falloff that tapers into the night side. dim: how much of the sky behind the air goes for each unit of its optical depth, so a star at the bright edge is dimmed. dimHeight: camera heights above the deck in radii between which the dim goes away on the way down, none below the first and whole from the second on. Below 0.4 radii the close picture brings its own glow above the limb in (closeup.json lay.glow: a share of 0.03 at 0.3 radii, 0.18 at 0.2, whole at 0.03), and the dim darkened that glow on the globe side only, which was a step at the handover (the report's side difference at T: mean 0.79 of 255 with the dim, 0.5 allowed). So the dim is gone before that glow counts, and it still holds while the last corner of the hold's sky is in the frame (to 4723, 0.30 radii). The ring is not sky: where it lies in front of the air on the line of sight nothing is taken from it, so its bands run across the limb unbroken. All of it by the weight of near, and by the share the view is away from the hold's.

cirrus.how: The footprint with which the opacity of the globe's cirrus is read in the dive and the rise. px: in pixels of a frame 1080 high (the set scales it by the height of the frame that is drawn, so it is one angle, 1/540 of the frame's height, at 1920 wide and at 3840 wide). The set takes the larger of this and the hold's 1 (look.ts clouds.soft), so at 1.0 the law is void and the cirrus is read with one footprint at every height, the hold's (ruled on 26 Nov: a law that does not cure is not kept). height: camera heights above the deck in radii, the law whole below the first and none from the second on. Why 1.0: round 39 set 2.0 against clouds that break into blocky square patches at 4707. Read on 26 Nov at review tier (28 samples of the shutter) with 1.0, 1.25, 1.5 and 2.0, the pale bars with square ends at x 1470 to 1525, y 570 to 615 stand at all four, nearly alike. Their cause is not the footprint. A thin cloud line of the map is a small steep piece of opacity; the frame moves 16.46 px across its open shutter (11.2 px along the row at that place); and the stop's shutter opens and shuts at once (handover.shutterEnds of config/showcase.json does not name neptune), which by the engine's own text at samplesFor draws a small light that moves as a bar with hard ends. At more than one sample the engine also reads every lookup at half a pixel, so at review tier the four footprints were half a pixel to one pixel in each sample. The trial of 26 Nov with the entry the other stops have ({share 0.5, fromPx 6, toPx 14}, laid for the render only) shows the bars gone at 4707 at review tier and the draft frame the same bytes; the entry is a shared file and comes from its owner. The footprint only cost the finest band of 4707 at draft (0.6 to 1.2 px against the approved close picture: 0.950 at 1.0, 0.836 at 1.25, 0.754 at 1.5, 0.625 at 2.0; main 0.947).
